# Five Things to Watch on Sunday \| Chiefs vs. Falcons

## Here’s a quick game preview heading into Sunday

Nov 14, 2026 at 02:27 PM

![Author Image](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_thumb_squared/f_auto/chiefs/s3swyzeiqravigmhffwh.jpg)

[Matt McMullen](https://www.chiefs.com/author/matt-mcmullen)

Senior Team Reporter

[Opens Twitter profile page in new window - Opens new window](https://twitter.com/kcchiefs_matt)[Send an email to mmcmullen@chiefs.nfl.com ](mailto:mmcmullen@chiefs.nfl.com)

- [Share on Facebook](https://www.chiefs.com/news/five-things-to-watch-on-sunday-chiefs-vs-falcons-x8239 "Share on Facebook")
- [Share on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Five+Things+to+Watch+on+Sunday+%7c+Chiefs+vs.+Falcons&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.chiefs.com%2Fnews%2Ffive-things-to-watch-on-sunday-chiefs-vs-falcons-x8239 "Share on Twitter")
- [Send email](mailto:?subject=Five%20Things%20to%20Watch%20on%20Sunday%20|%20Chiefs%20vs.%20Falcons&body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.chiefs.com%2Fnews%2Ffive-things-to-watch-on-sunday-chiefs-vs-falcons-x8239 "Send email")
- Copied!

The Kansas City Chiefs travel to Atlanta this weekend to take on the Falcons.

Here are five things to keep in mind heading into game day.

**1\. Here's a look at the final injury report for both teams.**

The Chiefs will be without right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) on Sunday, meaning Josh Ezeudu will likely make his second start of the season. Kansas City also won't have defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck stinger) for a second straight game.

Additionally, tailback Ken Walker (groin) won't play on Sunday. The veteran tailback reported groin tightness on Friday morning and was held out of Friday's practice. Walker was then initially listed as "Questionable" before being ruled out on Saturday.

Kansas City listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and running back Jaydn Ott (hamstring) as "Questionable" for Sunday, too. It's also worth noting that defensive tackle Chris Jones (personal) didn't travel with the team on Saturday, but he's expected to make it to Atlanta on his own and does not have a game desingation.

In some good news, wide receiver Xavier Worthy appears to be good to go after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over New York.

As for the Falcons, they'll be without rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) on Sunday. Branch has primarily contributed as a return man on special teams this year. The Falcons will also likely be without starting linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), who is listed as "Doubtful."

Additionally, Atlanta listed a pair of impact players as "Questionable" for Sunday's game in edge-rusher James Pearce (back) and defensive tackle Gervon Dexter (illness). Pearce, who registered double-digit sacks a year ago, made his season-debut last week. Dexter, meanwhile, ranks second on the Falcons with 25 pressures.

> Here's the final injury report for the Chiefs and Falcons. [pic.twitter.com/hdDTzyLpUY](https://t.co/hdDTzyLpUY)
>
> — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs\_Matt) [November 13, 2026](https://x.com/KCChiefs_Matt/status/2121344762254881022?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

**2\. Kansas City will need to find a way to contain running back Bijan Robinson.**

The top priority for the Chiefs' defense on Sunday is pretty simple: Kansas City has to find a way to at least contain Bijan Robinson's production.

In many ways, Robinson has mirrored what Ken Walker has done for Kansas City this year.

Both Walker and Robinson are near the very top of virtually every applicable leaderboard, including rushing yards (Robinson is first, Walker is second), total yards from scrimmage (Robinson ranks first, Walker ranks fourth), rushing yards-per-game (Walker ranks first, Robinson ranks fourth), broken tackles (Walker ranks second, Robinson ranks third) and average yards-per-rush (Walker ranks second, Robinson ranks fourth).

In other words, consider everything that Walker has been for Kansas City this year – that's what Robinson has meant to Atlanta. In simple terms, when Robinson has rushed for 145+ yards this year, the Falcons are 2-0. When he falls short of that number, Atlanta is 1-5.

Kansas City did an excellent job of containing Robinson back in Week 3 of the 2024 season, when the Chiefs held him to just 31 yards on 16 carries, and they'll need to find a way to turn in another strong effort on Sunday. It's also worth noting that Robinson ranks second on the Falcons in terms of targets (with 40) and will be a frequent component of Atlanta's passing game.

As for the Chiefs, Walker (groin) won't play on Sunday, and while his absence is significant, rookie tailback Emmett Johnson has flashed his immense potential in limited chances this season. He's likely to carry the load on Sunday, and there's no reason to believe that he isn't ready for the opportunity.

**3\. Creating pressure on Falcons quarterback Michael Penix is critical.**

Penix has often flashed the magic this year that made him one of the top players in all of college football not too long ago, such as his three-touchdown performance against San Francisco that dealt the 49ers their only loss of the year.

An area where Penix has struggled, however, is when under pressure. According to ESPN Research, Penix has completed a league-low 18% of his passes when pressured this season, and looking at last week specifically, he completed just 1-of-9 passes for -3 yards and an interception while under pressure.

Fittingly, Kansas City is coming off one of its best games of the season in terms of pressuring the opposing quarterback. The Chiefs racked up a season-high five sacks against New York last week, recording a 50% pressure rate according to Next Gen Stats.

It shouldn't have come as too much of a surprise, either. The Chiefs have been delivering a strong pressure rate for much of the season, they just didn't have the sacks to show for it. In fact, Kansas City's 9.8% pressure-to-sack rate through Week 8 was the lowest in the NFL. The Chiefs bumped that number up to 26.3% on Sunday, hopefully marking a sign of things to come moving forward.

**4\. Wide receiver Drake London has accounted for 39% of the Falcons' receiving yards.**

In addition to creating consistent pressure on Michael Penix, the Chiefs will need to find a way to at least contain wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons in targets (68), catches (44), receiving yards (692) and receiving yards-per-game (76.9) while averaging 15.7 yards-per-catch.

Notably, London has accounted for 39% of the Falcons' receiving yards as a team this year, and while he's likely to make some plays throughout Sunday's game, the Chiefs will need to find a way to at least limit the 6-foot-4, 215-pound London's production.

**5\. Atlanta's defense can get after the passer.**

The Falcons rank 20th in terms of scoring defense (24.8 points allowed-per-game) and 14th in sacks (20), but don't let those numbers fool you – this team is capable of causing some problems in the passing game.

Four different members of the Falcons have recorded at least 20+ pressures this year, as defensive linemen Brandon Dorlus (26), Cameron Thomas (26), Gervon Dexter Sr. (25) and Samson Ebukam (20) have each reached that tally. That group also doesn't include edge-rusher James Pearce, who made his season-debut last week after recording double-digit sacks a year ago.

The Falcons have often amassed those numbers without blitzing, too, as their 19.4% blitz rate is the fifth-lowest in the NFL.

One way to keep a strong pass-rush off balance is by running the football though, and for what it's worth, Atlanta has allowed at least 120 rushing yards in four of its last five games.

The Chiefs have topped 150 rushing yards as a team five times already this season, and – even without Ken Walker – their collective ability to run the ball effectively on Sunday may very well decide the game.

# Rules & Scoring ## NFL Classic In salary cap contests, participants will create a lineup by selecting players listed in the Player Pool. Contest results will be determined by the total points accumulated by each individual lineup entry (scoring rules summarized below). Participation in each contest must be made only as specified in the Terms of Use. Failure to comply with these Terms of Use will result in disqualification and, if applicable, prize forfeiture. ### Scoring | **Offense** | | --- | | Passing TD | +4 Pts | | 25 Passing Yards | +1 Pt (+0.04 Pts/ Yards) | | 300+ Yard Passing Game | +3 Pts | | Interception | -1 Pt | | Rushing TD | +6 Pts | | 10 Rushing Yards | +1 Pt (+0.1 Pts/Yard) | | 100+ Yard Rushing Game | +3 Pts | | Receiving TD | +6 Pts | | 10 Receiving Yards | +1 Pt (+0.1 Pts/Yard) | | 100+ Receiving Yard Game | +3 Pts | | Reception | +1 Pt | | Punt/Kickoff/FG Return for TD | +6 Pts | | Fumble Lost | -1 Pt | | 2 Pt Conversion (Pass, Run, or Catch) | +2 Pts | | Offensive Fumble Recovery TD | +6 Pts | | **Defense** | | --- | | Sack | +1 Pt | | Interception | +2 Pts | | Fumble Recovery | +2 Pts | | Punt/Kickoff/FG Return for TD | +6 Pts | | Interception Return TD | +6 Pts | | Fumble Recovery TD | +6 Pts | | Blocked Punt or FG Return TD | +6 Pts | | Safety | +2 Pts | | Blocked Kick | +2 Pts | | 2 Pt Conversion/Extra Point Return | +2 Pts | | 0 Points Allowed | +10 Pts | | 1 – 6 Points Allowed | +7 Pts | | 7 – 13 Points Allowed | +4 Pts | | 14 – 20 Points Allowed | +1 Pt | | 21 – 27 Points Allowed | +0 Pts | | 28 – 34 Points Allowed | -1 Pt | | 35+ Points Allowed | -4 Pts | ### Scoring Notes - Points Allowed (PA) only includes points surrendered while DST is on the field - doesn't include points given up by team's offense (e.g. points off offensive turnovers). - The following scoring plays will result in Points Allowed by your Defense/Special Teams: - Rushing TDs, Passing TDs, Offensive Fumble Recovery TDs, Punt Return TDs, Kick Return TDs, FG Return TDs, Blocked FG TDs, Blocked Punt TDs - 2pt conversions - 2 Point Conversion/Extra-point Returns - Extra-points - Field-goals - A fumble recovery will be awarded to a Defense/Special Teams if the team's offense recovers a fumble by the opposing defense (e.g. after an offensive turnover). ### Lineup Requirements Lineups will consist of 9 players and must include players from at least 2 different NFL games. The 9 Roster positions are: | | | | --- | --- | | 1 | QB | | 2 | RB | | 3 | WR | | 1 | TE | | 1 | FLEX
(RB/WR/TE) | | 1 | DST | ### Player Pool The Player Pool will consist of all NFL players expected to be on the active roster for any team scheduled to play in the contest Game Set. Occasionally a player may be missing from the Player Pool due to trades or other unforeseen circumstances. Each player listed in the player pool has an assigned salary and a valid lineup must not exceed the salary cap of $50,000. Due to the fluid nature of rosters, in the event a team adjusts their roster after player pools are finalized, DraftKings reserves the right to adjust player pools after contests for that Game Set have become available. In these instances, additional players may be added to the Player Pool up until 48 hours before a Game Set’s lock. This may result in valid lineups becoming invalid. Any participants who have entered contests for the Game Set prior to the adjustment will be notified via email. A "Game Set" is a set of games used for contests; each contest is tied to one Game Set. Contests tied to the same Game Set can be created at different times. Therefore, game policies are based on the timing of a Game Set being made available, not each individual contest. ### Position Eligibility Player positions are determined at the sole discretion of DraftKings. ### Lineup Edits Lineups may be edited at any time leading up to games. Each individual player will become "locked" at the scheduled start time of their team’s game. A locked player cannot be added or removed from a roster spot. Locked roster spots for all entries are displayed in contest GameCenters. If the scheduled start time for a game changes after contests for a Game Set containing that game become available, DraftKings will take measures to ensure the change is reflected on Draft Screens and for lineup editing purposes. In the rare case that a game starts before the scheduled start time, all players within that game will become locked as soon as our feed reflects that the game has begun. Additionally, any swaps that were made after the real-life start time of the game will result in those lineups being disqualified and refunded. ### Cancelled, Postponed, and Rescheduled Games In the event that a game is cancelled or postponed & rescheduled to a time within the original Scoring Period and this change is made less than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, the game will be included in the Game Set and players listed to play in that game will be eligible to accrue points. If a game is rescheduled for a time OUTSIDE the original Scoring Period and this change is made less than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, the game will be disabled from the Game Set and players listed to play in that game will NOT be eligible to accrue point. Players who you selected for your roster as of the time of the lock of the disabled game will remain in your roster and will accrue zero points. Players in disabled games will become locked at the originally scheduled start time of their game. The Scoring Period for NFL is defined as the timeframe between the scheduled start of the first game within the Game Set and 11:59pm ET on the first Wednesday after the last scheduled game within the Game Set. In the event that a game is cancelled or postponed & rescheduled to any time (both outside & within the original Scoring Period) and this change is made MORE than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, it is at the sole discretion of Draftkings to include or remove the game from that given Game Set. In the event a game is postponed, Draftkings will make a decision no later than 11:59pm ET of the day of the game on how to handle the postponed game. DraftKings may choose to adjust the Scoring Period for a Game Set at their sole discretion to accommodate schedule changes to any time before 12:00am ET on the day after the Game Set is scheduled. Any games that are disabled will be indicated as such on Draft Screens. Emails and other notifications may also be used to notify users of disabled games. If canceled or games rescheduled for a later date result in a Game Set including only one active game, then all contests for that Game Set will be canceled and refunded. Games are "known" to be canceled or postponed once their status is updated as such by DraftKings’ NFL stats-provider, STATS LLC. Example: If a Game Set includes two games at 8pm ET and 10:30pm ET respectively, and the 10:30pm ET game is officially postponed at 6pm ET then all contests for that Game Set are canceled and refunded. If the 10:30pm ET game was not officially postponed until after 8pm ET then contests for that Game Set are not canceled and are played out using only the one active game. If canceled or rescheduled games result in a Game Set including zero active games, all contests for that Game Set will be canceled and refunded. ### Suspended or Shortened Games DraftKings uses official NFL statistics and only includes statistics from games NFL deems to be official. If the NFL declares a game "suspended" then the statistics generated before the game is suspended will count in Game Sets containing said game. Any statistics generated on a later date when the game resumes will not be included. In the event that a game is suspended due to an injury or other "Act of God" type instance (determined at DK's sole discretion), and the game does NOT continue by the end of the scoring period (defined as 11:59PM ET on the first Wednesday after the last scheduled game within the game set), the following applies: 1. If the game is part of a multi-game set (such as Classic), all stats accrued up until the time of stoppage will count toward the set. 2. If the game is part of a single game set (such as Showdown), the following will apply: 1. If the suspension occurs in the first half of the game, the set will be refunded. 2. If the suspension occurs at halftime, or in the second half of the game, the set will be paid out as scored at time of suspension. ## Simulated NFL Classic ### Game Settings - Difficulty: All-Madden - Game Style: Arcade - Event Type: Exhibition - Even Teams: Off - Quarter Length: 8 minutes - Accelerated Clock: On - Play Clock: 20 seconds - Depth Charts found [here.](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/09/05/draftkings-madden-stream-depth-charts-for-all-teams-in-madden-27/) Note: In contests that are streamed where commentators are incorporated, the commentators are not in the same room as the game system device, and do not access to the game controllers. The actions of game operations or commentators cannot alter the outcome of the simulation. ### Stream Links Games are available for viewing in Game Center under the submitted lineup. Additional streams can be found on [Twitch](https://www.twitch.tv/draftkings/), at [DK Nation](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2024/07/22/madden-streams-information-page-3/), and on [YouTube.](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMJAKnrVv1sRzlq_vqige3Q) ### Game & Stream Malfunction Policy In the event of a game malfunction, all Game Sets with the affected match up will be cancelled and refunded. A game malfunction is defined as any malfunction that prohibits the game from finishing. There are rare instances in which there may be a malfunction of the DraftKings stream, but the game itself remains unaffected. In these cases, the streams will be completed offline. Gamecenters will update at the end of each quarter in these scenarios. DraftKings will publish the box scores of these contests, and all scores will be considered final after confirmation of all scoring plays and turnovers by our operations team.

expectations.subject: James Cook III
expectations.statement: Retain the leading Buffalo rushing role if active; do not expect another 31 carries or a receiving floor.
expectations.support: 31 Week9 carries versus Davis2/Johnson1; one receiving target.
expectations.uncertainty: Game script, short week and goal-line/QB allocation can change volume.
expectations.challenge: A shared or reduced rushing role, or injury restriction, challenges the selection.
expectations.observe: Compare carries/targets and team volume, actual active status; snaps/routes only if verified.

expectations.subject: Los Angeles Rams DST
expectations.statement: Garrett continues participating after his verified return if available; current opponent QB/center/WR problems are conditions to recheck, not a turnover forecast.
expectations.support: Primary report35/58snaps and6pressures/27rushes in return; MichaelWilsonseasonOUT, Minshewtests/Froholdtprotocol.
expectations.uncertainty: Rams own offensive injuries and McDuffie uncertainty; rookieQBnotconfirmed, normalfullworkloadnotassumed.
expectations.challenge: Garrett setback/restriction, Arizona protection/starter resolution or further Rams coverage loss before cutoff.
expectations.observe: Verify active participation and available snaps/pressure; separate sacks/turnovers/TDs/PA after games.

expectations.subject: Rashee Rice
expectations.statement: Continued meaningful receiving involvement is required to support the $6,100 selection; a Worthy absence is not assumed to increase Rice's routes.
expectations.support: Seven retained Week9 targets, but PFF below67% route participation in each of last two games and Armstrong taking five of six late post-injury plays.
expectations.uncertainty: Worthy designation and Week10 rotation/route allocation; Mahomes elbow.
expectations.challenge: Current participation/role reporting or game route involvement shows Rice losing opportunities; separate QB performance from receiver deployment.
expectations.observe: Postgame targets and qualified route participation if accessible; missing routes remain unassessable, not inferred from catches.

expectations.subject: Tank Dell
expectations.statement: Continue meaningful receiving participation in the outside rotation if active; no full-time role or repeat63-yard score expected.
expectations.support: ESPN9targets/4-105-TD; PFF33snaps/22routes/55%routes, but8targets in its chart.
expectations.uncertainty: Outside rotation and target-source coverage; high target rate may recede.
expectations.challenge: Dated rotation evidence or game participation shows a minor role, even if a touchdown masks it.
expectations.observe: Qualified snaps/routes and targets relative to Houston passing opportunity; separately report coverage and explosive-play points.

expectations.subject: Tyler Warren
expectations.statement: Remain a meaningful Colts receiving participant despite offensive personnel turnover; no guaranteed gain from departed WRs.
expectations.support: Retained7targets plus officialAllen/Downs departures; Nelson also traded.
expectations.uncertainty: Replacement receiver allocation, protection and absolute team passing volume.
expectations.challenge: Lower route participation or team pass opportunity after protection changes; targets do not automatically transfer.
expectations.observe: Targets/routes if available, team attempts/yards and protection evidence separately from touchdowns.

expectations.subject: KC Concepcion Jr.
expectations.statement: Remain a meaningful Browns receiving participant with Watson starting, rather than needing a repeat64-yard touchdown.

expectations.subject: Emmett Johnson
expectations.statement: With Walker ruled out, Johnson is expected to receive meaningful lead rushing opportunity if active; no exclusive backfield or fixed touch floor assumed.
expectations.support: Primary Saturday report rules Walker OUT; dated team preview expects Johnson to carry the load.
expectations.uncertainty: Ott questionable, replacement execution/protection and game script; reporter expectation not a coach usage guarantee.
expectations.challenge: Other backs dominate opportunity or Johnson is materially limited/inactive.
expectations.observe: Official carries/targets and team rushing distribution; snap/route shares only if available, otherwise unknown.
